messages:
Maya: Hey team — Fluxly onboarding flagged intermittent high latency during last night's ramp. Need a short playbook we can send them for how we report SLOs and when credits apply. Can @Li confirm metrics + exact window we should show? (cc @Devon)

Omar: I saw the alert at 02:13 UTC, p95 spiked to ~1.2s for ~9 minutes. Oncall link: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-5987> :rotating_light:

Li: yep — digging in now. Looks related to autoscaler not adding nodes because GPU quota was hit; we fell back to a lower-throughput pool. Pulling the exact numbers and will paste them.

Maya: Thinking the customer-facing playbook should be: 1) what happened, 2) impact (uptime + p95 numbers), 3) remediation and timeline, 4) whether credits apply, 5) next steps for preventing recurrence. Does that align with finance/legal?

Devon: Finance note: credits only kick in if the committed monthly uptime SLO is missed. For Fluxly the contract commits 99.95% uptime. Latency targets (p95 300ms) are performance objectives but not creditable in this contract. Still worth showing latency trend.

Omar: Quick calc from the alert: incident duration ~9 minutes. Monthly window = 30 days -> 43,200 minutes. Downtime 9 / 43200 = ~0.0208% drop. So uptime would be ~99.9792% — above 99.95, so no credit.

Li: Metrics snippet I'm pasting for the note:

```
SLO window: 30d
Total window minutes: 43200
Downtime minutes: 9
Resulting uptime: 99.9792%
Committed SLO: 99.95% -> no credit
p95 baseline: 280ms -> incident p95: 1.2s
```

Maya: Perfect. For the customer email I want a short concise paragraph and a chart. Can someone draft the one-paragraph explanation and a suggested chart caption? I'll attach the metric gif. Also want an enablement bullet for renewal conversations so they don't over-index on a single blip.

Devon: I'll draft the customer-facing paragraph now. Suggestion: "We observed a short period of elevated latency due to autoscaler quota exhaustion which temporarily routed traffic to a lower-throughput pool. Your committed uptime SLO of 99.95% was not breached; no service credits apply. We’ve implemented monitoring and will add an autoscaler quota alert and runbook step to proactively notify your CS team."

Omar: Ops/Eng action items to include in internal playbook: 1) add quota-exhaustion alert (severity medium) 2) audit autoscaler fallback path + reduce cooldown 3) add CS notification step when fallback occurs. Assigning to @Li.

Li: I’ll take items 1–3. ETA: EOD tomorrow for alerts + runbook update.

ops-bot: Incident INC-5987 annotated: autoscaler quota event -> https://redwood.internal/incidents/5987 (linked runbook updated).

Maya: Thanks all. Devon send your draft by 10:00am PT and I’ll review and send to Fluxly by noon. I’ll also add a 1‑pager for renewal enablement that explains how uptime vs performance metrics are treated for credits. Closing loop once sent. :thumbsup:
